style_context: Hand wood carving, carving tools, sharpening, wood grain, and small carved project techniques

images.description: Close-up instructional photo of clean splinter removal from a fingertip using fine-point tweezers, grasping the splinter close to the skin and pulling in the same direction the splinter entered, with simple callouts for tweezer tip, pull direction arrow, and hand position, neutral background, no branding or visible text beyond short instructional labels
images.value: Shows the exact tweezer position, grip near the skin, and pull direction that text alone cannot teach clearly

images.description: Clean educational diagram of a carving knife held at a steady bevel angle on a flat sharpening stone, side view with one horizontal arrow showing stroke direction and brief labels for blade bevel, sharpening stone, and steady angle, uncluttered workshop-style background, no branding
images.value: Shows the bevel angle and stroke direction relationship that text alone cannot convey precisely

images.description: Three-panel educational diagram of a V-cut in wood, showing first angled knife cut, second angled knife cut, and finished V-shaped groove, each panel with simple horizontal labels and clean wood cross-section view, minimal text, no branding
images.value: Shows how two separate angled cuts meet to create one clean groove, a sequence that text alone cannot visualize well

images.description: Four-panel progress diagram of a simple in-the-round wood carving project such as a neckerchief slide or small figure, moving from rectangular wood blank to rough shape, refined form, and finished rounded carving, consistent viewpoint, clean educational style, minimal labels, no branding
images.value: Shows how an in-the-round project changes shape across stages, a visual progression that text alone cannot communicate clearly

images.description: Three-step educational diagram of chip carving a single triangle from a flat wood board, showing first cut, second cut, and third cut releasing the triangular chip, top-down view with simple arrows and minimal labels, clean wood surface, no branding
